title: EC2 Fundamentals
description: Learn EC2 basics, instance types, AMIs, key pairs, security groups, and user data.

data.text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) is AWS's foundational compute service. It provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud. With EC2, you can run applications just like you would on a physical server, but with the ability to scale capacity up or down in minutes.

data.title: Elastic Means Flexible
data.text: The elastic part of EC2 means you can start with one server and quickly add more when demand increases, then remove them when demand drops. You only pay for the time you use.
AWS offers many instance types optimized for different workloads. The naming convention follows a pattern: family, generation, size, and optional capabilities.

An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is a pre-configured template that contains the operating system, application server, and applications needed to launch an instance. Think of it as a snapshot of a server ready to be cloned. When you launch an EC2 instance, you choose an AMI.

A key pair is used for secure login to Linux instances or to decrypt the Administrator password for Windows instances. AWS stores the public key, and you keep the private key safe. Never share your private key.

A security group acts as a virtual firewall for your EC2 instance. It controls inbound and outbound traffic. Security groups are stateful: if you allow an inbound request, the response traffic is automatically allowed back.

terms.definition: A virtual server in AWS that you can launch, configure, and manage.
Amazon Machine Image — a pre-configured template used to launch EC2 instances.
A set of security credentials used to authenticate and connect to EC2 instances.
A virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic for EC2 instances.
Scripts or commands that run automatically when an EC2 instance first boots.

data.text: User data lets you run scripts automatically when an EC2 instance first starts. This is useful for installing software, configuring settings, or pulling the latest version of your application.

data.title: Launching an EC2 Instance with AWS CLI
data.content: This example shows how to launch a t3.micro instance in us-east-1 with a key pair and security group.
data.code:
# Create a key pair and save the private key
aws ec2 create-key-pair \
  --key-name my-key-pair \
  --query 'KeyMaterial' \
  --output text > my-key-pair.pem

# Create a security group allowing SSH (port 22)
aws ec2 create-security-group \
  --group-name my-ec2-sg \
  --description "Allow SSH access" \
  --vpc-id vpc-12345678

aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress \
  --group-id sg-12345678 \
  --protocol tcp \
  --port 22 \
  --cidr 203.0.113.0/24

# Launch an EC2 instance
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --image-id ami-0abcdef1234567890 \
  --count 1 \
  --instance-type t3.micro \
  --key-name my-key-pair \
  --security-group-ids sg-12345678 \
  --subnet-id subnet-12345678 \
  --user-data file://user-data.sh

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: EC2 provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud
Instance types are optimized for specific workloads
AMIs are templates used to launch instances
Key pairs authenticate access to instances
Security groups act as virtual firewalls
User data runs scripts automatically on first boot
